newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: NAB falls on weak third quarter result.
newsitem.headline: NAB falls on weak third quarter result.

text.p: Shares in Australia's biggest bank National Australia Bank Ltd (NAB) fell over two percent following a weak third quarter profit result.

By 12.03 p.m. (0203 GMT), NAB shares were 43 cents lower A$19.07 after the result which showed profit from the Australian operations was down 15 percent in the June quarter, compared with the March quarter.
The shares were trading at A$19.45 before the results' announcement.

"It (third quarter) came in below market expectations and now we are seeing the market reacting," said one Melbourne-based broker. The broker said there might be some switching into other banks such as Commonwealth Bank and ANZ.

NAB reported a net profit of A$504 million for the three months to June 30, compared with A$505 million in the same quarter a year earlier. But, NAB reported a 9.3 percent rise in net profit to A$1.645 billion in the nine months to June.
The broker said this share price fall was likely to get the bank's halted share buy-back scheme put back onto the agenda.
